summary:
We developed Health Assistant Agent, an onboard AI assistant that helps astronauts monitor their health and decide what to check first. It brings together cabin sensor readings, wristband data on pulse, sleep and movement, and crew mood check-ins.

Our prototype uses archived NASA ISS cabin CO₂ readings and simulated crew data. In the demo, two astronauts report headaches while a cabin air reading is missing. The assistant spots the gap and asks the crew to check the air record and tell the medic. Both symptom reports stay in the log after the reading returns.

On long missions, astronauts may need to act before Earth can respond. The assistant keeps working during a communications outage, giving the crew a clear next step and a record they can share when contact returns.
details:
Health Assistant Agent helps astronauts see what has changed and decide what to check first. On a spacecraft, cabin sensors and wristbands would send readings with the time they were taken. A radiation badge would record dose, the exercise machine would log resistance training, and crew members could enter their own mood check-ins. Our prototype replays nine real ISS cabin CO₂ readings from NASA’s Rodent Research-1 archive and uses simulated readings for the other sensors.

The assistant checks for missing or old readings. A small onboard model compares pulse, sleep and movement with each astronaut’s usual values and looks for similar practice cases. The app explains why it suggests a check and gives a crew SOS first priority.

In our drill, Earth goes offline, two astronauts report headaches, and one cabin air reading is missing. The assistant asks the crew to check the air record and tell the medic. When the reading returns, both symptom reports stay open. This gives the crew a way to act during an outage and a record they can use to brief ground support when contact returns.

We built the prototype with HTML, CSS and JavaScript and packaged demos for Android and macOS. The onboard assistant runs offline. The web version supports a larger AI review through the OpenAI API when the link is up and an API key is configured. ChatGPT and Codex helped with development.

We designed around three conditions the crew may face: lost communication, missing sensor readings, and the need to keep personal information private. Mood check-ins stay in the open app view, and the crew medic makes medical decisions.
